_comment: BiblioCommons library systems (mapsee_ingest_bibliocommons.py). One entry per library; `slug` is the tenant name in both gateway.bibliocommons.com/v2/libraries/<slug>/events and <slug>.bibliocommons.com. No key and no account. `city` and `country` are read only by catalog_curate's coverage report - the adapter ignores them - and they are here because two of the six systems are Canadian, which the report was counting as American. `category` is only the fallback for a programme whose type and audience say nothing - most rows classify themselves, and library programming is overwhelmingly learning and kids. Every row arrives with a surveyed branch coordinate, so nothing here is geocoded; see the adapter header. Counts below were read live on 2026-09-03 and are recorded so a later run can tell a quiet library from a broken one. The 38 systems added 2026-09-24 carry `measured_2026_09_24`: programmes the adapter itself KEPT inside a 90-day horizon (58,629 between them), not the gateway's total. 90 rather than 180 because that batch is three times the size of the first six and lands in one sync step with a 20-minute limit; a library programme is listed well inside 90 days of happening, so the window rolls forward and loses nothing but distance.

_why: Probed 2026-09-03 with the production User-Agent and NOT configured.
Recorded so nobody spends another curation run rediscovering them -
`_not_included` is an editorial no, and anything proposing sources must
THE 403s BELOW ARE A REFUSAL AND ARE TREATED AS ONE. The library is on
BiblioCommons and its catalogue answers; the events gateway specifically
returns 403 to this User-Agent. That is a `no`, not an obstacle: it was
not retried with a browser User-Agent and it must not be. The DICE note
in ../mapsee-aggregator/CLAUDE.md is the same rule - a door somebody has
closed is closed even when you can see the handle.
If any of these are wanted, the way in is to ASK the library, which is
what venue outreach is for. Several of them publish an events iCal on
their own site as well; that belongs in ics_sources.json, not here.
